author: sjm41
body:
* **ARBA rule (ID and label):**
ARBA00000900

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel FBgn0034411	CG18605	(A0A0B4JD40)

* **Description of issue**
CG18605 lacks any identifiable InterPro domains so is unlikely to be an active enzyme.
However, ARBA00000900 assigns EC:2.3.2.27, presumably based on a FunFam match. I doubt this is true.
title: ARBA2GO issue: ARBA00000900

author: claude[bot]
source_title: Review ARBA00000900: E3 ligase rule with complexity issues

author: Antonialock
body: This comes from panther signature PTHR46077. In panther, I only see [one drosophila gene](https://www.pantherdb.org/panther/family.do?clsAccession=PTHR46077) in this group, topors. However in uniprot we currently have two drosophila proteins in this group, topors and CG18605. CG18605 has lost the N-terminal E3 ligase region. I suspect this annotation will disappear once we have updated our panther family annotation (that seems reasonable to assume?). The gene has however been published (minimal phenotype characterization) so I could probably get it into SP, the paper should be quick to do in any case.

author: sjm41
body:
Thanks @Antonialock 

I made a ticket for the related PAINT (PTHR46077) issue, back in Feb 2023:
https://github.com/geneontology/go-annotation/issues/4463

But as you say, it seems the current PTHR46077 family doesn't contain CG18605 (A0A0B4JD40) anyway, so the issue I reported will go away when UP incorporates the current PANTHER release (or you curate the protein into SP).

That will fix this specific issue I reported, but it seems this is just reflecting a bigger issue with the ARBA rule, from the Claude analysis you (or someone else?) posted above.

author: Antonialock
body: yes I saw the age of the PAINT ticket! 3 years seems a long time & that the change should have trickled through. I curated the entry so it should disappear for all affected drosophila entries (I think it is a drosophila specific proteins, at least it seemed like it was absent in mosquito).

author: sjm41
body: I think the fix on the PAINT ticket at the time was just to block the IBA annotation to CG18605 (A0A0B4JD40), not a change to the PANTHER family itself. I assume the PANTHER family change happened more recently.
